speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; please tell me you have come in because of a skin concern, and describe the specific lesion you are worried about, including how long it has been present and how it has changed.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning presentation, especially given your significant smoking history and the location of these lesions; have you noticed any bleeding, rapid growth, or pain in either the penile or finger lesion?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the penis and digit.

The history of chronic non-healing, crusty lesions in an immunocompromised-appearing host with heavy smoking history is highly suspicious for malignancy rather than simple infection or eczema. I need to confirm the extent and rule out other differentials immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile lesion and finger lesion. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of penile and digital lesions.
